newsitem.title: DENMARK: British BSE crisis hits Danish MD Foods result.
newsitem.headline: British BSE crisis hits Danish MD Foods result.

text.p: MD Foods International A/S (MDI), one of the world's biggest exporters of dairy products, said on Friday it swung back into the red in 1995/96 due largely to the BSE (mad cow disease) crisis and a price war in its key British market.

"Although we expect an improved 1996/97 result, it will take a few years before the rationalisation of our UK operations and the costs involved in that are over and MDI can again post a positive result," the group said in a statement.
The overseas arm of dairy co-operative MD Foods, MDI posted a 216 million crown deficit for 1995/96, compared to 1994/95's 13.1 million crown surplus.
It attributed its loss to price pressure in the British retail sector, negative consequences of the BSE crisis on milk prices and major rationalisation costs.

"Given the rationalisation and market measures we have already carried out, (British subsidiary) MD Foods Plc is well placed to meet competition and develop in the next few years," MD Chief Executive Jens Bigum said in a statement.
MDI had annual turnover of 3.7 billion crowns, 80 percent of which was in Britain, with the rest in Saudi Arabia, South Korea and Brazil, where MDI has subsidiary companies.
MD Foods group as a whole posted a net profit of 590 million crowns on turnover of 21.022 billion crowns for the year 1995/96.
